tasks.Title: The 11 highest peaks of the Dolomites
tasks.ShortDescription: Flight around the Dolomites' 11 highest peaks, with some rain and beautiful rainbows along the way.
tasks.LongDescription: The inspiration for the flight comes from a video posted by @Topher420247 in the "soaring" channel that gave me the idea of a trip around the 10 (well 11 here) highest peaks of the region.($*$)($*$)Make sure to use the weather preset but verify that the wind layers are all set to 115 degrees @ 11 knots. ($*$)($*$)Also, we’ve had gorgeous landscapes / weather when taking off at 3:15 PM (August 1st if that makes a difference). And press B to adjust your altimeter for the correct pressure, or you won’t make it to the required altitudes.($*$)($*$)If you take the time to get high enough (11k ft) before the start, I’d say it should be easy. If you get stuck at some point loosing too much, then it can get harder, thus the intermediate… some places are tricky but you can still do it, just takes some time. ($*$)($*$)Note: you may encounter « see-through » bugs with some of the mountains in this flight, where the mountains seem to « deconstruct » themselves. Seems like an MSFS bug for all we know.

tasks.Title: SSC Concepción AAT
tasks.ShortDescription: An AAT task near Concepción in Argentina. Fly over a mountain to get to the desert thermals on the other side.
tasks.MainAreaPOI: Concepcion and surrounding mountains and deserts
tasks.LongDescription: Take of from runway 02 at Concepcion Airfield, find a cloud that takes you above Start height at 6000ft.($*$)($*$)WP1 is in a mountain face, you will need to climb over and to the other side of it, the wind is 15kts from NE so it should be easy.($*$)($*$)Reaching the desert, find a good route thru the clouds that takes you deep into WP2.($*$)($*$)On the way back to the Finish, you need to go over some high terrain with a headwind, the ridges to the north are doable aren't that great so manage your altitude and plan well.($*$)($*$)Good luck and happy flying!

tasks.Title: Diamonds - Jan Mayen
tasks.ShortDescription: Sightseeing ridge soaring on Jan Mayen volcanic island up North in the Arctic Ocean.
tasks.LongDescription: Sightseeing ridge soaring on Jan Mayen volcanic island up North in the Arctic Ocean. ($*$)($*$)The date and time is on purpose, as the sun gets low on the horizon and then back up again.($*$)($*$)The choice of glider set for the task (ASK 21) is just to indicate that you should be flying this with a slow glider, to enjoy the landscape in this relatively short task.($*$)($*$)Basically, the goal is to fly to the SE tip to the NW tip, covering the total length of the island, while also climbing to the top of Beerenberg volcano, the highest peak at about 7500 feet.($*$)($*$)Have fun!

Located on top of a mountain at  2,430 meters (7,970 ft), in the middle of a tropical forest, it is considered the tourist attraction par excellence in Peru.($*$)At WP3 there are breathtaking views of the second highest mountain in the Cusco region, known as Salkantay, whose name in Quechua means "wild mountain" and reaches an altitude of 20,574 feet (6,271 meters). Get high before you get there.
tasks.WeatherSummary: There is good wind and thermal clouds. Use them!

tasks.Title: Diamonds - Bobaye Mt. Nepal Trek 280
tasks.ShortDescription: Bobaye Mt. Nepal Trek
tasks.LongDescription: This is a site seeing trip to some great mountains in Nepal. A suggestion is to get high early and stay high. The altitude envelope recommendations are 15k to 18k on the first half of the trip and 14k to 17 K on the second half. Try to stay near to the task tracks. You will need at least 17200ft in the middle of leg 1 to 2, and between leg 2 and 3. WP 4 is the Bobaye Mt. Take your time here it is some great scenery. Watch out for the max altitude at WP 5.

tasks.Title: A Tribute to The Blue Ridge Soaring Society
tasks.ShortDescription: Typical low level but fast ridge track flown by gliders around VA85 in Virginia.
tasks.SimDateTimeExtraInfo: Very important to get the amazing sunrise and fog
tasks.RecommendedAddOnsList: [{"Name":"We love VRF region 2","URL":"https:\/\/flightsim.to\/file\/16674\/we-love-vfr-region-2","Type":"Freeware"},{"Name":"Powerlines and solar farms","URL":"https:\/\/flightsim.to\/file\/26186\/powerlines-and-solar-farms","Type":"Freeware"},{"Name":"Project Litfts Europe ","URL":"https:\/\/flightsim.to\/file\/14840\/project-litfts-europe ","Type":"Freeware"}]
tasks.LongDescription: It's early in the morning, on a nice August day, the sun will rise in about 15 minutes, there's a nice fog in the valley, but clear sky with just a few clouds way above the mountains. Winds are from the NNW, strong enough to go ridge surfing and do some tree-top scraping! Yep, this is a very low flying course, while enjoying a nice sunrise.($*$)($*$)Fill up those ballast and launch from runway 36 at VA85, home of the BRSS (Blue Ridge Soaring Society). Don't need to go very high on that launch, we'll hop right on to the ridge to the left of the airfield. Don't forget to go through the Start at a maximum altitude of 4000 feet.($*$)($*$)Now, simply surf the ridge all along the waypoints! Go as fast as you can while keeping as low as 50' to the trees, a little higher if you want to feel safer, but watch for the maximums at each gate. tasks.LongDescription: I've found a freeware scenery for a gliding club we've not flown at - so lets load up the trailers and take a trip! This is notionally a 343km task, but since it's an Assigned Area Task (AAT) it could be anything from 178km to 531km! Given we're mostly mountain flying, and the weather forecast is for decent conditions including some great thermal climbs, if you're taking one of the big gun gliders, you can expect you'll need to fly 250+km to occupy yourself for this flight that has a MINIMUM FLIGHT TIME of 1h15min.($*$)($*$)This should be a fun flight, with some decisions in front of you - some big, some not so big, but they all might have big consequences later in the day. First up, you have to plan how you're going to get to the start line, which is a 15km odd journey into rising land. Are you going to catch and climb in the thermals to reach the maximum starting altitude, or are you going to catch what you can and hit the ridge to top up your height - but if you do that you have to backtrack a bit to the start line ! Oh dear... :) ($*$)After that, how are you going to attack hitting your next waypoint - fly the ridge lines as much as you can, or head into the steeper terrain. And where are you going to push onto before making the turn to the next waypoint? That's the joy (or torture) of an AAT. Enjoy :) ($*$)($*$)If you're new to AATs, here's an explanation from @vrflybob for everyone who may not be familiar with them.($*$)($*$)Here is a brief outline of how an AAT works:($*$)Just like a normal task you need to visit each Waypoint in the correct order.($*$)You can choose how far or how little into each waypoint you travel.($*$)An AAT task may have a minimum time.($*$)The winner has the highest average speed - distance divided by time, where:($*$)Distance is not your track length, but a straight line calculation of the farthest point you went into each waypoint relative to the adjoining waypoints.($*$)Time is your actual task time or the minimum AAT task time, whichever is greater (there is no penalty for going over time).($*$)($*$)I also have a few simple tips - nothing earth shattering but might be worth revisiting. ($*$)* Fly longer than the assigned minimum flight time, even if it's only seconds, but don't plan to be home early - use the last waypoint to absorb more time if you need by flying further into the WP.   ($*$)* The idea is to fly the *fastest* so that means picking directions into the "areas" that are hopefully going to give you the best flying conditions. Pick a "turning point" that gives you good chances of thermals (eg cloud streaks) or that allows you to use ridge lines to fly faster. ($*$)* Spend a little time (but don't go overboard and obsess) looking at the map and figuring out where you might fly and what features might influence your flight path.($*$)* Fly into all waypoint "areas" at least part of the way. Don't just kiss the circle unless you're already over time and you have not much chance of improving your average speed and you're just trying to get home. ($*$)See you outside the Lethbridge hangar!

tasks.Title: Alexandra to Queenstown
tasks.ShortDescription: NZLX to NZQN
tasks.SoaringExtraInfo: Thermals may be present but not really worth chasing.
tasks.LongDescription: Launch from Alexandra and follow the ridges up North to Omarama then turn West. Get onto the same ridge we used to summit Aoraki but this time turn South. Take in the views of Lake Hawea (Turnpoint Dingleburn Station), Lake Wanaka (Nearby airfield famous for Warbirds Over Wanaka air show) and ski resorts approaching Queenstown. At Queenstown the main airfield is designated as your landing area but a smaller airfield is close by and is more glider friendly (no big jets). Also there are plenty of paddocks around but don't try the Golf Course! It's a mountaineering exercise to play that one! It's worth staying airborne around Queenstown to explore the area anyway. No race, no rush, take your time to enjoy!

tasks.LongDescription: **This is a race - Rules below**($*$)Launch from The Coves Airport West of Hartebeestpoort Dam (Hartebeest is a large antelope, poort is a gorge or canyon) and gather to the East of the start line at Nadia's Peak, elevation 1660m, start gate maximum 1700m. When the start gate opens at 21:15Z go through it and begin the race. Next is P1858, a peak at elevation 1858m then Gifkoppie (Poison hill or head) and Olifantsnek (Elephant's pass) with Olifantsnek dam on your left. Be careful here, get this one wrong and it could poison your race time! On to Maropeng, the Cradle of Humanity where the highest concentration of ancient remains of the earliest modern humans have been found. This may  mean that we are all South Africans or decended from South African ancestors! Getting to this point again requires some strategy. The ridge South of the Magaliesburg is lower and has lower promenence so the lift is not as good. Shortly after passing P1533 is a little Southward extension of the Hartebeespoort dam. Look right to Pelindaba (Zulu for end of story, Pelile Indaba), the site of South Africa's uranium enrichment facility. The actual enrichment plant is called Valindaba which means We don't talk about this! The buildings are not modelled in the sim. On to Pretoria. Here we are very close to the Pretoria CBD and the ridge is disapearing into the landscape. More decisions and on to Mamelodi, home to a famous Soccer stadium. On to Wonderboom Reserve (Wonder tree, a type of fig tree, specifically the individual in the reserve over 1,000 years old covering a huge area) then P1532, see if you can spot the cable car between them, and  the finish over Nadia's Peak car park. Land anywhere you like, there are 6 airfields, at least one golf course and landable fields everywhere within reach.($*$)($*$)**Rules:**($*$)1. Winner is the person who crosses the finish line earliest after adding penalties and deducting bonuses.($*$)2. Start gate opens at 21:15Z($*$)3. 2 second per second penalty for an early start($*$)4. half a second per second bonus for a late start($*$)5. 1 minute bonus for flying the LS4($*$)6. 10 minute penalty for flying anything 18m with an additional 5 minute penalty for the DG808($*$)7. 2 second penalty for each second over Vne($*$)8. proof of flight will be a screenshot of your task page and a flight log readable in B21's task planner (https://flightsim.to/file/15872/simflightpath). Failure to complete the flight is automatic disqualification. Also if the 15m tips note is not visible in your screen shot rule 6 will apply!($*$)9. Rules, as unreasonable as they may be, are not negotiable($*$)10. have fun!

tasks.Title: FSC - Alpine Odyssey - Leg 6
tasks.ShortDescription: To continue the Alpine Odyssey, use the glider you started with!($*$)LIMW to LSGR
tasks.DifficultyExtraInfo: Mostly easy but a few tricky bits need some skills!
tasks.LongDescription: Ballast up, this task needs a bit of speed. Launch from Aosta using any means you like, (Gravity roll not available, sorry!) go through the start and climb the hill to the North. Once through the guide waypoints at the top head to the next ridge to the North. This forms the Swiss/Italian border and favours fast ridge running while leading to some of the highest peaks in the Alps. First is Dent D'Herens (try to arrive close to the peak's altitude). Around the corner is the Matterhorn which we climb again but perhaps on a more favourable wind. Of course there's a minimum! Next 4 thousander is Breithorn then Liskamm, Ludwigshohe, Punta Gifnetti, Dufourspitze , all part of the Monte Rosa Massif with Dufourspitze the highest. On to Strahlhorn, Rimpfishhorn, Weissmies, Dom, Weisshorn and Aletschhorn for a total of 13 peaks over 4,000m. Approaching Balmhorn dump your ballast, you won't need it for the fast high final glide to Fruitingen and landing at Reichenbach. If you think we are done with high peaks wait for the next leg of our journey!
